coverage_of_risk.rationale: No tests exist at all, and the untested surface is precisely the high-risk one: data transformation, filtering/pagination, URL state and 404 paths.

behaviour_not_implementation.rationale: The rubric scores 'no tests' at 1; there is nothing behavioural or otherwise.

evidence: app/app/lib/pokeapi.ts:75-89 — api() caches the promise, so a rejected fetch is cached forever; a refactor here would fail silently with no test to catch it
app/app/pages/pokemon/[name].vue:33-90 — version-group selection default, method ordering (METHOD_ORDER), level-up sort: a one-character change (e.g. b.order - a.order) would pass unnoticed
app/app/pages/index.vue:70-74 — dropping the 'omit defaults' rule or breaking page clamping would surface only if the acceptance suite happens to cover that combination
regression_power.rationale: With no tests in app/, any regression outside the acceptance suite's exact assertions ships undetected; the data layer is the single point of failure for five pages.

evidence: app/ — 0 test files, 0 cases (confirmed by grep across app/ excluding build output)
signal_to_noise.rationale: No tests means no noise, which the rubric scores as 3 — but it also means zero signal.

findings.issue: No test infrastructure whatsoever: no test script, no devDependencies, no runner config; the app's only guard is the harness-owned acceptance suite.
findings.suggestion: Add @nuxt/test-utils v4 + vitest v4 (the current Nuxt-recommended stack) with a 'test' script; start with unit tests for lib/pokeapi.ts, which needs no Nuxt environment at all.

findings.issue: speciesCardsForRefs implements the alt-form exclusion (>10000), dedupe and dex-sort rules used by three page types; it is untested, and a subtle bug (e.g. dropping the seen-set) would double-list Pokémon on /moves, /abilities and /types.
findings.suggestion: Table-driven unit tests with fake refs including ID 10033 (Mega) to pin the exclusion and dedupe behaviour.

findings.issue: humanize, idFromUrl, latestEnFlavor and englishName encode spec-critical formatting (Mr Mime, #0025, whitespace collapsing, last-English-entry) as untested regex/loop code.
findings.suggestion: Pure-function unit tests: humanize('mr-mime')==='Mr Mime', idFromUrl with and without trailing slash, flavor text containing \f\n, empty names array.

findings.issue: URL state round-trip is untested and subtly fragile: the debounced watch on q pushes the same query the route-watcher just synced from, which can create spurious history entries on back/forward; page clamping (Math.min) and default-omission in buildQuery are also unguarded.
findings.suggestion: Tests that set /?q=&type=&page=999 and assert the resulting URL and rendered 'Page n of m'; and a back/forward navigation test to pin history behaviour.

findings.issue: The moves pipeline (default game = highest order, ?game= override, grouping by method, Level-Up by level-then-name, method order) is ~60 lines of the most intricate logic in the app with no tests.
findings.suggestion: Extract this into a pure function (input: pokemon + version-group records; output: games/methods) and unit-test the ordering rules and the unknown-method fallback (localeCompare branch).

findings.issue: Missing-values-sort-last in both directions and aria-sort toggling are behaviour the acceptance suite only spot-checks; a refactor that flips the missing-first branch would regress unnoticed.
findings.suggestion: Component test via mountSuspended asserting row order after clicking Power twice, and aria-sort values on all headers.

findings.issue: api() caches promises including rejections: one transient API 500 poisons that URL for the server process lifetime, and nothing tests this failure mode.
findings.suggestion: Cache successes only (delete from cache on rejection), and add a test that a failing fetch is retried on the next call.

findings.issue: Not-found handling (404 status on SSR, NotFound rendering) and the non-404 error path (api() throws on 5xx, yielding Nuxt's error page without the banner/contentinfo landmarks) are untested.
findings.suggestion: An e2e test with a stubbed API asserting both the 404 page for /pokemon/missingno and the error page still renders the required landmarks.

findings.issue: SSR reads process.env.API_BASE_URL at request time while the client relies on runtimeConfig; a mismatch would break hydration, and this is untested.
findings.suggestion: A runtime test asserting the server-injected state matches what the client sees.

findings.issue: The hand-rolled concurrency limiter (waiters queue, shift on finally) is untested; a bug in waiter wakeup would deadlock all SSR fetches under load with no test to catch it.
findings.suggestion: Unit-test limited() with MAX_CONCURRENT exceeded, or replace with a small well-tested library util.

summary: The app ships zero tests of its own — no runner, no script, no devDependencies — leaving ~660 LOC of data-layer and URL-state logic guarded only by the harness's acceptance specs. The riskiest code (species index building, alt-form filtering, pagination/query sync, the moves grouping pipeline) is exactly what's untested, so the first refactor of the data layer will be flying blind. Nuxt's current recommendation (@nuxt/test-utils v4 + Vitest v4) would cover the pure functions in lib/pokeapi.ts almost for free, which is the obvious first step.
